name: Master of Liberal Arts

rules.name: Requirements Overview
rules.desc: Candidates for the MLA degree must complete a minimum of 50 units of coursework with at least a grade point average of 3.3 (B+). These units must include a three-quarter foundation course (equal to 12 units total), one 4-unit core introductory seminar for second-year students, at least seven 4-unit graduate seminars (six of which must be MLA-specific seminars), and a six-unit master’s thesis. Students must also fulfill distribution requirements in the following areas: humanities; social science or social policy; and science, medicine, or engineering.

rules.name: Foundations Courses
rules.desc:
During the Autumn, Winter, and Spring quarters following admission to the program, a three-quarter foundation course sequence (equal to 12 units total) is required of all students, MLA 101A Foundations I, MLA 101B Foundations II: the Middle Ages and Renaissance, and MLA 101C Foundations III: the Enlightenment through Modernism. This course sequence aims to lay the groundwork for the interdisciplinary, intercultural studies the student will shortly undertake. The foundation course introduces students to the broad framework of history, literature, philosophy, political science, and art.
Foundations and Core Seminar courses must be completed with a minimum 3.3 grade point average.

rules.name: Core Seminar
rules.desc:
During the first quarter of the second year, students take the 4-unit core introductory seminar, MLA 102 An Introduction to Interdisciplinary Graduate Study. This seminar prepares students for interdisciplinary graduate work at Stanford. Students concentrate on writing a critical graduate paper, conducting library research, presenting the results of their research, and productively participating in a collaborative seminar.
Foundations and Core Seminar courses must be completed with a minimum 3.3 grade point average.

rules.name: MLA Seminars
rules.desc: Students must take at least seven graduate seminars of four units each over their second, third, and fourth years in the program; these can be fulfilled by MLA seminars for all seven courses, or by taking six MLA seminars and one (approved) Stanford departmental graduate seminar. Within the required MLA seminars, students must also complete at least one seminar in each of the following areas: Humanities; Social Sciences; Science, Engineering, and Medicine. Each MLA course requires a substantial seminar paper. Students are encouraged to use these papers as a way to investigate new fields of interest, as well as a way to develop different perspectives on issues in which they have an ongoing interest. MLA seminar offerings vary yearly, and those listed below may not be available in future years. The 2026-2027 curriculum is included below.

rules.name: Program Milestones

children.name: Thesis Prospectus approved by the MLA Faculty Advisory Committee

rules.desc:
Students are required to fulfill the following milestones:

• Application for Active Student Status. The first nine quarters represent a probationary time for each MLA student. To be eligible for active student status, within nine quarters a student must have successfully completed the Foundation Sequence, the Core Seminar, and the first two seminars with no incompletes, with a minimum 3.3 (B+) grade point average, and must have complied with all University policies and procedures. Upon completion of their second seminar, students must submit the Application for Active Status.

• Thesis Prospectus. Students who are ready to begin the thesis process (consult eligibility requirements in the MLA Handbook) must submit their Prospectus for approval by the MLA Faculty Advisory Committee. Students should use the Declaration of Intent to Proceed/Prospectus form.

• Colloquium. Students completing their thesis work are required to present their work at a colloquium open to the MLA community. The colloquium consists of a 35-minute talk about the thesis followed by a 10-minute response from a pre-selected respondent, and a 15-minute question-and-answer session. Details about the Colloquium process are available to students in the MLA Thesis Instructions document.

rules.name: 3.3 (B+) GPA overall and in the Foundations and Core Seminar courses
Thesis Requirement
rules.desc: Students are required to complete a 75-100 page thesis with the guidance of an assigned faculty advisor. While students are working on their theses, they should enroll in MLA398: Thesis in Progress each quarter until their final quarter. Students should enroll in the six-unit MLA399: Thesis Final Quarter in their final quarter.

gpa: MLA students must maintain a 3.3 (B+) grade point average overall in courses applicable to the degree.
grading: MLA students must earn a B- or better grade in all courses applicable to the degree.
policies: MLA students must complete the Foundations and Core Seminar courses (first year and one quarter of study) with a 3.3 or better grade point average in order to move on to taking MLA seminars. MLA students must complete the first six courses of study (Foundations I, II, III, MLA 102, and two seminars) within nine quarters.
transferPolicy: The MLA does not accept transfer credits.
reviewNotes: The audit checks 50 units, each course with a B- or better: the three Foundations courses, MLA 102, seven 4-unit graduate seminars (one each in Humanities, Social Sciences, and Science, Engineering and Medicine, plus four more), and MLA 398 and MLA 399. Checked by hand: the 3.3 GPA overall and in the Foundations and Core Seminar, active student status within nine quarters, the thesis prospectus, the thesis colloquium and the thesis, and one approved departmental graduate seminar if you take one in place of an MLA seminar. Transfer credit is not accepted.
